evals.prompt: Write the YouTube title and description for our hackathon demo. Project is TalkTuahBank, voice banking over a phone call. Won 1st Overall at HackUTD 2024. The 2-minute video goes: 0:00 intro, 0:15 the problem, 0:40 live phone call demo, 1:30 architecture, 1:50 wrap. Devpost is devpost.com/software/talktuahbank, repo at github.com/aurelisajuan/TalkTuahBank.
evals.expected_output: Two or three title options, a full description with a strong first-two-line hook, valid YouTube chapters, tags, and a pinned comment.
expectations: The chapters start at 0:00, are in ascending order, and there are at least three of them.
The description front-loads the hook in the first two lines and includes the Devpost and GitHub links.
The title references the real award and no fabricated awards or stats appear.

evals.prompt: I need a YouTube description for my demo video but I haven't written down the timestamps yet. The project is a CLI tool for generating test data. Read the repo for details.
evals.expected_output: A description and title that read the repo, and either ask the user for the video beats or explain how to get them rather than inventing timestamps.
expectations: The skill does not fabricate chapter timestamps; it asks the user for the video beats or how to derive them.
It reads the repo before asking for missing facts and invents no awards.
It still produces a title and a description hook suited to a CLI tool.
